stemMd: In the second paragraph, buyers "will discount every bottle accordingly." As used here, "discount" most nearly means that buyers

options.label: A
options.textMd: refuse to buy any bottle whose quality they cannot check.

options.label: B
options.textMd: sell bottles on to other shoppers at a lower price.

options.label: C
options.textMd: ignore the price and rely on the taste of the oil.

options.label: D
options.textMd: reduce what they are willing to pay, allowing for the chance that the oil is poor.

options.label: E
options.textMd: ask each seller for a reduction on the price shown in the shop.

explanationMd:
For meaning-in-context questions, set aside the sense you know best (a shop's discount) and reread the sentence around the word. The whole sentence is: if buyers cannot tell good oil from mediocre oil, "they will offer a price that reflects the average quality they expect, and they will discount every bottle accordingly". The buyers are the ones acting, and what they do is lower the price they offer because they doubt the quality. To "discount" a bottle is therefore to value it at less than its best case, allowing for the chance of disappointment.

Check by substituting each choice into the sentence and reading on. The next sentences say the price offered falls and careful producers are paid less than their oil is worth, so buyers are still buying, at a lower valuation. Refusing to buy would leave no price to fall; haggling with each seller brings in a bargaining scene the passage never describes; reselling turns the buyers into sellers; and relying on taste is impossible, since the passage says quality can be judged only after paying.

distractorRationale.e: This gives "discount" its everyday shop meaning, a reduction the seller grants at the till. In the passage no one bargains: the buyers themselves lower what they are prepared to offer.
distractorRationale.a: Buyers in the passage still buy, at a lower price. Refusing to buy would leave no market in which the offered price could keep falling, as the paragraph says it does.
distractorRationale.c: Buyers cannot taste the oil before paying, which is the whole problem the passage describes, and the paragraph is about the price they offer, so it is not ignored.
distractorRationale.b: This reads the buyers as traders passing bottles on. Nothing in the passage concerns resale; the buyers are shoppers deciding what to offer.

accessibilityText: A meaning-in-context question about the olive oil passage. It asks what "discount" most nearly means in the second-paragraph phrase "they will discount every bottle accordingly". The five choices say that buyers: refuse to buy any bottle whose quality they cannot check; sell bottles on to other shoppers at a lower price; ignore the price and rely on the taste of the oil; reduce what they are willing to pay, allowing for the chance that the oil is poor; ask each seller for a reduction on the price shown in the shop.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Buyers offer a price based on the average quality they expect, so they lower what they will pay for every bottle to allow for the risk of poor oil. E is the literal shop-discount trap. A contradicts the fact that buyers still make an offer. B and C have no support. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: Buyers 'offer a price that reflects the average quality they expect', meaning they lower what they will pay to allow for the risk of poor oil. A is contradicted, because buyers still buy at the average price. B and C have no support. E reads 'discount' literally as haggling over a shop price, which is not the economic sense used here.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: only the reading in which buyers lower their own valuation fits the sentence and the next sentences, in which the price offered falls. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
